newsitem.title: USA: Britain determined to get fiscal deficit lower.
newsitem.headline: Britain determined to get fiscal deficit lower.

text.p: Britain is well on the way in the crucial reduction of its fiscal deficit, Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Saturday.

"When you look at the health of the British economy compared with the other major economies of Western Europe we are well on course to get our public finances moving towards balance," he told reporters following a meeting of the Group of Seven finance ministers.
Clarke said he was not trying to set policy to meet either the Maastricht criteria or guidelines from the International Monetary Fund.
Maastricht criteria anyway coincided with what any British Conservative would consider sound financial policy.
"I'm setting British fiscal policy to achieve balance in the medium term. I believe it is very important to get our fiscal deficit down to a sustainable level," he said.
"It's very important to stop the stock of debt to gdp rising. All this is for the good of the British economy."
He added that the IMF view of the UK's fiscal position was barely any different from Britain's own, he added.
